summary: The core is built like the Capcom board: Capcom-style H/V raster counters drive scan-time tile and sprite fetches, sprites are DMA-copied over the Z80 bus with BUSRQ/BUSAK and then scanned per line into a pair of line buffers, and layer priority is a lookup in the bd01.8j PROM. MAME instead draws per frame from buffered spriteram in reverse order and uses a guessed split_table for tile priority. Only the memory/port map, register bit meanings and tilemap address layout match MAME, and a correct core has to share those anyway. The shared jtgng_* modules are a Capcom-family library with per-game LAYOUT cases, not a MAME transliteration.

findings.note: Each pixel builds an 8-bit address {char opaque, obj opaque, scroll prio bits, scroll colour} that indexes the bd01.8j PROM, and the PROM's selbus output picks the layer and the palette-bank bits. MAME uses a hand-guessed 16-entry split_table plus transmask groups and a fixed bg-low/sprites/bg-high/text draw order.

A write to port 6 (OKOUT) starts a bus request. Once BUSAK arrives during vblank, a counter (blcnten) drives the main RAM address and copies sprite RAM into the object buffer. MAME maps port 6 to the watchdog and copies the buffer for free on vblank.

findings.signal: Per-line sprite scan with a hardware limit
findings.note: For each line, a SEARCH/TRANSFER machine walks the DMA buffer, uses an adder (Vsum, top bits ANDed) to test whether a sprite is on that line, and copies at most OBJMAX_LINE (32) sprites into a line-object RAM. MAME loops over all sprites once per frame from offs = bytes-4 down to 0, with no per-line limit.

H counts 0x80-0x1FF and V reloads from 250 at H=511. Blanking, HINIT (H==0x86) and a separate object-timing LVBL_obj two lines early are all decoded from those counter values, rather than from screen raw parameters.

findings.signal: Scroll fetch from H/V counter bits
findings.note: Scroll position is added to the flipped H/V counters every pixel, including the board-style H7 term (~H[8] & (~flip^HF[6]))^HF[7]. HS[2:0] phases set when the tile/ROM address is latched and when the 4bpp planes are shifted out.

A CPU access to scroll or char RAM raises busy while HS[2:0]<2, and the busy signal stretches the Z80 clock enable. This models the board's arbitration between the CPU and video fetches, which MAME does not emulate.

findings.signal: Flip and sprite X MSB done in board style
findings.note: Flip is an XOR on VF and on the line-buffer write address, and attribute bit 4 (hover) becomes bit 8 of a 9-bit position. MAME computes sx = x - ((attr&0x10)<<4) and sx = 240 - sx.
INT1 is set on a main-CPU write and cleared by an MCU port-3 bit 1 output, and LVBL is wired to a port-3 input. MAME clears INT1 inside the from_main_r read handler and connects no vblank pin.

findings.signal: Sprite pipeline split into board-like blocks
findings.note: The sprite engine is split into DMA, line-object buffer, a draw counter chain (over/objcnt/pxlcnt incremented as one register), ROM depacking, and a line buffer pair. This follows the board's stages, not MAME's single draw_sprites function.
The address decode and the inverted CHRON/SCRON/OBJON bits match MAME, as any correct core must. The decode itself is a casez on A[15:13]/A[12:11] chip selects, not handler functions.

The 8x4/4x8 layouts are the same address mapping as MAME's mapper callbacks. Here they are bit concatenations of V/H counter bits selected by the latched layout register, so the shared part is data layout, not structure.
